claims.claim: The canonical Internal CSPRNG production profile implements HMAC_DRBG with SHA-256 and a requested 256-bit security strength.
claims.qualification: Source review, deterministic vectors, one traceable NIST CAVP response vector, and focused runtime QA support the claim. It is not NIST validation.

claims.claim: The selected HMAC_DRBG SHA-256/256 application implementation is structurally conformant with the applicable SP 800-90A Rev. 1 state transitions and request envelope.
claims.qualification: Assumes correct .NET HMAC implementation and OS/runtime behavior. Two LOW exceptional-path/audit findings remain and formal validation has not occurred.

claims.claim: Mosera enforces a maximum of 65,536 bytes per Generate request and the 2^48 reseed interval.
claims.qualification: Boundary tests verify allowed/rejected values and unchanged state after precondition rejection.

claims.claim: The production profile requests 48 OS entropy bytes for Instantiate, 32 OS bytes for nonce, and 48 fresh OS bytes for immediate reseed per draw.
claims.qualification: This states requested byte counts and call behavior, not min-entropy.

claims.claim: The production provider uses OS cryptographic entropy APIs and fails closed when acquisition or readiness fails.
claims.qualification: Linux getrandom, Windows BCryptGenRandom, and macOS SecRandomCopyBytes are application trust boundaries. Host/kernel integrity and source quality remain external.

claims.claim: Every canonical Internal CSPRNG draw has isolated session state and no cross-draw shared Key/V state.
claims.qualification: Runtime services are stateless and the provider creates and destroys one session inside each generation call.

claims.claim: Bounded integers and Keno/Matrix/Pick transformations avoid modulo bias and preserve their defined sampling semantics.
claims.qualification: Reviewed logic uses unsigned rejection sampling, explicit big-endian conversion, partial Fisher-Yates, and positional with-replacement arrays.

claims.claim: Canonical Internal CSPRNG outcome generation is exactly once, durable, replay-verifiable, manifest-bound, and certificate-bound without provider fallback.
claims.qualification: Focused full-chain QA demonstrated same-draw concurrency, restart recovery, result reuse, certificate binding, settlement handoff, and rejection of Official/Manual fallback. Cancellation attempt audit completeness remains LOW risk.

claims.claim: New provider evidence persists no raw entropy, nonce, reseed material, Key, V, DRBG state, or secret-derived SeedIdentifier.
claims.qualification: Migration 119 versions the contract and leaves historical version-1 evidence interpretable and immutable.

claims.claim: Mosera implements formal SP 800-90A prediction-resistance request semantics.
claims.qualification: Per-draw instantiation and immediate reseed are not the standard prediction-resistance request interface.

claims.claim: Mosera has a 256-bit SP 800-90B validated entropy source or proven 256 bits of min-entropy.
claims.qualification: SP800_90B_VALIDATION_NOT_ESTABLISHED. Byte count and API success do not prove min-entropy.

claims.claim: Mosera is formally conformant with a final SP 800-90C construction profile.
claims.qualification: SP800_90C_CLASSIFICATION_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. RBG2 is the closest structural candidate, subject to entropy and module-boundary evidence.

claims.claim: The NIST CAVP response vector makes the implementation CAVP or CMVP validated.
claims.qualification: The vector is internal test coverage only; no validation certificate exists.

claims.claim: Mosera's Internal CSPRNG is NIST certified, independently audited, laboratory certified, or regulator approved.
claims.qualification: No independent assessment, laboratory certificate, NIST certificate, or regulator approval exists.

claims.claim: CSPRNG-1.2B directly statistically qualified source hash 53ecf20c...d30.
claims.qualification: The full campaign belongs to historical hash 0c2639d9...d46. The remediated hash has separately identified targeted regression evidence.

claims.claim: Best-effort zeroization guarantees physical erasure of all secret material in .NET and the host.
claims.qualification: Managed memory, JIT/runtime copies, cryptographic internals, dumps, debuggers, and host compromise remain outside that guarantee.

claims.claim: The current local Game Engine container image is the immutable remediated production artifact.
claims.qualification: The local image predates remediation and base image tags are not digest-pinned. A fresh attested image is required.
